status: Dependency analysis for the next batch only; no Bomb Grimace, supplied bomb or dependent boss implementation is claimed.

identity_correction.finding: There are TWO required external identities: unlit Throwable Bomb pickup 5.41.0 and bomb entity 4.13.0. Both share the animation but differ in collision mass/radius/grid-collision settings. The prior hazard preflight mentioned only 4.13.0. Neither is one of the 653 enemy/boss records.
identity_correction.scope: Keep typed pickup/bomb identities; do not invent extra enemy rows or collapse pickup state into a normal inventory bomb.

source_contract.unlit: Bomb Grimace keeps a throwable bomb available. The pickup cannot add ordinary inventory bombs.
source_contract.take: The bomb can be picked up and thrown; its fuse starts after pickup, not on initial floor supply.
source_contract.replenish: A few seconds after Isaac takes the bomb, supplier creates another. Exact delay and global-versus-per-producer stock ownership remain unmeasured.
source_contract.exceptional_death: Bomb Grimace emits ten Throwable Bombs on documented instant-death destruction. Generic execution is only a test hook; named item producers remain necessary.

current_engine_gaps: Simulation::deployDynamite always checks and decrements ordinary dynamite inventory. It is not the correct producer for free supplied bombs.

makeDynamite snapshots the player Braid item and starts an already-lit fuse. Whether source throwable bombs inherit each item effect is not established; do not silently inherit all player bomb modifiers.

Current hazards are cleared on room transitions; an unlit supplied pickup needs explicit per-room persistence. Carrying an armed bomb needs a defined transition policy without freezing or resetting its fuse.
Existing movement/gravity/collision can be reused after throwing. The pickup/carry/fuse/resource phases still need real state, input, visuals and tests.
Current Demolition tags distinguish spent inventory dynamite and rock waves. Add supplied-bomb provenance explicitly; do not label it spent inventory merely to enable demolition.
planned_state_contract: Unlit stock pickup with stable ID and supplier/room ownership; does not tick a fuse.
Taking transfers to at most one carried armed bomb and schedules replenishment. Replenishment is tied to taking stock, not to explosion; existing carried/thrown bombs may still be alive.
Carried bomb follows the player with a running fuse. Throw uses aim and current swept ballistic collision; fuse is preserved and can expire while held.
Explosion keeps source/ownership, terrain permissions and damage separate from normal inventory spending.
Exceptional supplier death queues ten valid pickup positions with bounded capacity. Re-entry must not accidentally duplicate stock or erase remaining drops.
control_adaptation_to_define: Provide both keyboard and mouse operation using existing interact/aim/attack controls, with carried-bomb use taking precedence over ordinary shooting. Preserve current place-dynamite behavior whenever no supplied bomb is held. This mapping is DeathWard control design, not a measured Isaac input contract.
validation_needed: Unlit pickup never detonates over a long wait; taking starts the configured fuse.
Pickup and throw work at zero inventory without changing inventory, ordinary shot count or copied bomb affixes.
Held fuse expires and damages the holder; throwing does not restart it.
Taking one supply schedules a replacement while previous bomb is still armed.
Two suppliers, exceptional ten-drop burst, global caps and blocked spawn sites remain deterministic and bounded.
Room leave/re-entry and carried transition preserve explicit state/clock ownership.
Throw hits cover and applies real armor/demolition effects through correct provenance.
Mandatory supplied-bomb encounters remain completable after supplier destruction/wasted bombs; any recovery rule is declared an adaptation.
dependent_encounters: Tuff Twins: two six-part armored chains, at least two suppliers, sourced armor/segment HP, explosive resistance and child-spawn conditions.
The Shell: two five-part flying chains, one or two suppliers, grounded exposed segments and detached-group behavior; split/new-head rule still needs clarification.
Mother's Shadow: dedicated escape sequence with temporary item/resource suppression/restoration and a continuously pursuing invulnerable entity.
rock_wave_scope: The pinned Tuff/Shell pages document armor-breaking rock waves created by named items (Mega Bean/Wait What?) and Terra. This does not establish that hostile Quake Grimace waves must damage those bosses. Implement item-produced rock-wave armor interaction separately; preserve ownership distinctions.
